title: sre-weekly-update-2026-03-14
content:
SRE Weekly Update - 2026-03-14

Owners and attendees: Jordan Lee (owner), Aisha Patel, Miguel Santos, Lina Chen, on-call rotation: week of 2026-03-09 was Miguel, handoff to Aisha for week of 2026-03-16.

Summary highlights:
- Major incident on 2026-03-10 (INC-2026-0310): Redis cluster failover + autoscaling misconfig caused elevated latencies for inference-api for ~45 minutes.
- SLO status: inference-latency p95 and error budget tracking below threshold, small burn from cache-miss spike.
- Runbook updates: redis failover playbook clarified, added checklist for capacity alarms and autoscaler cooling windows.
- On-call handoffs: added explicit note to pass pending escalation tickets and recent pager trends.

Incidents:
1) INC-2026-0310 - Redis cluster failover + autoscaler race
- Time window: 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC to 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC
- Severity: Sev2 (customer impact: increased 95th and tail latency on inference-api, elevated error rate to 1.8% from baseline 0.1%)
- Services affected: inference-api, prefix cache layer, rate limiting sidecar (transient)
- Summary: Routine maintenance triggered a Redis node replacement in prod-redis-primary. During the replacement, the autoscaler detected increased CPU pressure on inference workers and attempted to scale up. Due to a misconfigured cooldown period, multiple scale actions overlapped while the cache cluster was in read-only recovery mode, causing a storm of cache misses and thundering-herd traffic to model backends. This pushed request latency up, and some downstream timeouts bubbled to the API surface.
- Mitigation: Rolled back the autoscaler aggressive policy, increased autoscaler cooldown to 6 minutes, scaled a stable pool of warm inference instances, and promoted a recovered Redis replica to primary to finish failover faster. Restored normal traffic routing by 03:00 UTC.
- Root cause: combination of maintenance-triggered failover and a too-aggressive HorizontalPodAutoscaler policy without guardrails for cache recovery windows.
- Follow-ups / action items:
  - Update Redis failover runbook with explicit autoscaler pause step (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-03-16).
  - Add automated guardrail: HPA should consult cache readiness probe before scaling (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-03-28).
  - Create a synthetic test that simulates cache failover and validates autoscaler behavior (owner: Lina, due: 2026-04-04).
  - Postmortem draft link: CON-4321 (working draft, assign reviewers: eng-sre + serving-runtime).

2) INC-2026-0312 - Short spike in 500s from model backend pool
- Time window: 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC to 11:35 UTC
- Severity: Sev3 (no customer-visible downtime, increased internal error rates and retry storms)
- Notes: Investigation shows a GC pause on a subset of model servers after a memory regression in a recent runtime patch. Reverting the patch reduced 500s.
- Action: Reverted runtime patch, scheduled canary rollback check for next deploy cadence. Owner: Miguel.

SLOs and error budget
- inference-api latency SLO: p95 < 220ms, target 99.95%
  - Reporting window: last 7 days
  - Current compliance: 99.89% -> small burn (0.06% of error budget used this week primarily from INC-2026-0310).
- availability SLO: 99.99% monthly
  - No full outages this week, still within target but monitoring trend.
- Actions:
  - Schedule SLO review meeting with product and serving-runtime to discuss stricter cache readiness gating. Proposed 2026-03-22. Owner: Jordan.
  - Add automated alert when weekly error budget burn rate exceeds 30% of remaining budget. Owner: SRE tooling team.

On-call and handoffs
- Recent rotation notes:
  - Week 2026-03-09: Miguel (primary), Lina (secondary). Pager spike on 2026-03-10 at 02:10 UTC, fully handled by on-call with escalation to Jordan.
  - Upcoming week 2026-03-16: Aisha (primary), Miguel (secondary). Handoff checklist attached below.
- Handoff checklist (to include in Slack handoff message):
  - Active incidents and current status: link to postmortem draft CON-4321 and incident channel.
  - Pending on-call runbooks being updated and owners.
  - Any long-running investigations or pages suppressed.
  - Access notes: temporary keys or debugging hotfixes in use.

Runbook and tooling updates
- Added: redis-failover-autoscaler-step to runbooks repo. Short checklist to pause HPA during critical cache recovery windows.
- Alert tuning: raised threshold for cache-miss alert to reduce noisiness during scheduled maintenance; added suppression windows for scheduled deployment maintenance.
- Playbook change: emphasize communication between infra-maintenance and SRE before executing failovers that affect shared caches.

Standup / meeting notes (weekly SRE sync 2026-03-14)
- Attendees: Jordan, Aisha, Miguel, Lina, product-eng rep (Samira), support lead (Derek).
- Decisions made:
  - Prioritize autoscaler guardrail work (Miguel) and runbook update (Aisha).
  - Add synthetic cache-failover test to CI (Lina).
- Blockers:
  - Need access to historical HPA scaling events across clusters (infra telemetry) - request submitted (JIRA-SRE-1102).
  - Dependency: serving-runtime team needs to sign off on adding cache readiness probe to model pods.

Action items (short list)
- Aisha: finalize redis failover runbook update and publish (due 2026-03-16).
- Miguel: implement HPA guardrail patch and write unit tests (due 2026-03-28).
- Lina: build synthetic test harness for cache failovers and wire to CI (due 2026-04-04).
- Jordan: schedule SLO review (target 2026-03-22) and invite product + serving-runtime.
- SRE tooling: implement alert for weekly error budget burn > 30% (owner TBD, ticketed).

Notes to self / informal:
- Remember to follow up with infra on whether maintenance window can be moved to low-traffic UTC times.
- Investigate if we can pre-warm a small pool of read-only cache replicas during failover window.
- Ticket backlog looks ok but need to clear runbook PR queue before next on-call rotation.

Attachments and links:
- Postmortem draft: CON-4321 (Confluence)
- Scaling telemetry request: JIRA-SRE-1102
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/982

Status and next update:
- This doc is a draft. Will update postmortem links and close action items in next weekly update (2026-03-21).

-- End of update
